summary: Independently re-verified every claim in the software-engineer handoff for the /dashboard skeleton-flash fix, and added the one meaningful test that was missing. (1) Rendering mode: ran my own detached-worktree method (git worktree add ... HEAD --detach twice — 'baseline' at HEAD, 'modified' with the working tree's page.tsx/DashboardBody.tsx/layout.tsx-deletion copied in, node_modules symlinked), built both with pnpm build, diffed the full route tables and diffed prerender-manifest.json route keys. Confirmed: exactly one route-table line differs (`○ /dashboard` at baseline -> `ƒ /dashboard` modified), and `/dashboard` is the only route removed from the static prerender manifest (0 added). (2) Confirmed `/settings/page.tsx` at HEAD uses the identical cookies()-read-then-verifyIdToken pattern with no `export const dynamic` anywhere in the file (grepped for 'force-dynamic'/'export const dynamic' — no hits) and is `ƒ` in both my baseline and modified builds, which is the entire premise for omitting force-dynamic on /dashboard. (3) Diffed old HEAD:page.tsx against the new DashboardBody.tsx directly: every hunk is above the `return (` statement (header comment, DashboardData export, Props/SIGNIN_REDIRECT additions, FetchState seed, the auth-redirect effect split from the fetch effect, and the loading-guard restructure into `if (initialData === null) { ... }`). From `<main id="main-content" ...>` through the closing `SkeletonCard` function at end of file, there is zero diff — confirmed byte-identical, not eyeballed. (4) Traced the DashboardData shape field-by-field: `duelStats` narrowing in page.tsx emits exactly {wins, losses, current_streak, best_streak}, which is exactly DuelRecordCard's DuelRecordData interface (checked DuelRecordCard.tsx:14-19) — the raw getDuelStats()/Prisma DuelStats row also carries user_id and an updated_at DateTime (checked schema.prisma:835-841 and the API route, which passes the RAW un-narrowed row to NextResponse.json — so the server path is actually stricter/cleaner than the existing client-fallback API response, not a regression). freeClimb maps 1:1 to UserFreeClimbRecord/FreeClimbData (peakY, rank, totalClimbers, wins, handle — verified both interfaces match exactly). replays/recentDuels: ClimbReplaySummary.createdAt and RecentDuelItem.completedAt are declared and produced as `string`, not Date, by src/db/climb.ts and src/db/duel.ts respectively, so nothing un-serializable crosses the RSC server->client boundary. (5) Confirmed via `git show HEAD:app/app/dashboard/layout.tsx` that the deleted file was only the Metadata-workaround pass-through (11 lines, no other logic) and the identical `robots: {index:false,follow:false}` now lives in page.tsx. Grepped the whole app/ tree: nothing else imports the deleted layout.tsx, and DashboardBody is imported only by the new page.tsx. (6) Confirmed verifyIdToken is the single shared function (src/lib/firebaseAdmin.ts) also used by requireAuth.ts and by settings/page.tsx — not forked. (7) Confirmed /api/dashboard/route.ts, requireAuth.ts, firebaseAdmin.ts, authCookie.ts have zero diff vs HEAD. (8) Added app/tests/components/dashboardBody.test.tsx (3 tests, renderToStaticMarkup + mocked useAuth/useRouter, same pattern as tests/components/climbFeelSurfaces.test.tsx) asserting: real DuelRecordCard content renders on first paint when initialData is provided even while authLoading=true and token=null (the actual defect); the fallback path still shows the loading spinner when initialData is null and authLoading is true; and the signed-out-with-no-initialData path renders nothing (redirect in flight). Proved this is a real gate, not a placebo: temporarily reverted the FetchState seed to always start at {status:'loading'} (pre-fix behaviour) and re-ran the suite — test 1 went red with the exact defect symptom (two SkeletonCards render instead of the duel record), then restored the file and re-ran clean. Confirmed a non-test caller exists for DashboardBody (page.tsx) before trusting this test as coverage. All 6 context/gates.json gates re-run by me and green: app-lint (0 warnings), app-typecheck (clean), app-test (81 files / 748 tests, up from 80/745 — my new file), orchestrator-typecheck, orchestrator-test (58/58), pack-hygiene (0 violations). No app/next-env.d.ts churn in the main repo (all builds ran in separate detached worktrees, which I removed afterward via `git worktree remove --force`). Did not commit or push.
goal: Verify the /dashboard skeleton-flash fix: independently confirm rendering-mode claims, confirm JSX/data-shape correctness by diffing source directly, confirm no missed callers, add missing test coverage for the actual defect, and prove the full gate suite is genuinely green.

learnings.insight: app/tests/components/dashboardBody.test.tsx now exists and directly asserts the fixed defect (real content on first paint while authLoading, via renderToStaticMarkup with mocked useAuth/useRouter). It also confirmed something the handoff didn't call out explicitly: NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED is 'true' in this shell's process.env (not from a repo .env file — no .env.example entry, must be exported by the runner environment), so WalletCard actually renders (with token=null) in the server-populated first-paint case during local/CI test runs, not just in a hypothetical prod config. This is a real exercise of the caveat the software-engineer flagged (WalletCard mounting with a null token) and it renders safely (0 chips, no crash) — verified live, not just reasoned about.
learnings.action: If NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED ever flips in a given environment, re-run app/tests/components/dashboardBody.test.tsx — it exercises the WalletCard-with-null-token path for real whenever that flag is true, so it's a live canary for that interaction, not just a reasoning argument.

learnings.insight: For rendering-mode verification, building in two separate `git worktree add <dir> HEAD --detach` trees (one left untouched as baseline, one with the working tree's uncommitted files copied on top) and symlinking node_modules into each worked cleanly and left the main repo's app/next-env.d.ts untouched — no churn to revert. This is a strictly better pattern than building directly in the main repo (which the prior six cycles all had to revert next-env.d.ts for).
learnings.action: Prefer the two-worktree-build pattern for all future rendering-mode verification; it avoids the recurring next-env.d.ts churn entirely instead of reverting it after the fact.
